title: 内存水位机制：zone、min/low/high watermark 与保留页
key_conclusions: Zone watermarks explain when reclaim starts, while LRU and MGLRU explain which pages reclaim selects.
The healthy path is kswapd waking below low and reclaiming back toward high before app allocations enter direct reclaim.
Free memory must be interpreted per zone with reserves; global MemFree alone can hide low-zone pressure.
Watermark tuning requires before/after validation with zoneinfo, vmstat, PSI, lmkd logs, and user-visible jank evidence.
shallow_points: The article does not include real zoneinfo snapshots from specific Android devices.
It does not validate watermark_scale_factor and watermark_boost_factor availability across Android kernel versions.
It does not include a controlled experiment showing min_free_kbytes changes and direct reclaim deltas.
It does not quantify safe tuning ranges for different RAM classes.
discovered_connections: Day 49's reclaim path is governed by Day 50's watermarks: watermarks trigger reclaim, LRU/MGLRU select reclaim victims.
A low global MemFree signal is weaker than a zone-specific free/min/low/high comparison.
Direct reclaim, PSI, and LMKD pressure can begin after repeated watermark failures even before a Java heap looks large.
Watermark reserve policy connects kernel VM behavior to user-visible app jank and kill risk.
